text:
Sasha: Heads-up: scheduling a rolling maintenance window in euc1 for tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. Plan is staggered node drains + soft GPU reboots on pool-euc1-A and pool-euc1-B. Expect ~18 racks (~144 GPUs) to be cycled. Need backfill + latency plan.
Maureen: Ack. Any hard constraints on p95 latency we should use for routing thresholds?
Sasha: Primary SLO is p95 <= 220ms for interactive hosted endpoints. During the window we allow emergency bump to p95 <= 350ms for non-critical routes; critical routes must stay under 1s. We'll fallback to smaller-model variants if needed.
Lee: If we spill ~40% of active sessions to dedicated-pool-usw, estimate we need ~60 GPUs warm. That buys headroom but adds ~+$2.1k/hr in burst cost (rough calc).
Devon: Can we pre-warm KV cache on the receiving pool so requests don't cold-hit? I can run a seed job 30m before start.
Sasha: Yes — plan to run cache-seed + prefix warm on receiving pools. Also will enable conservative batching to smooth token throughput.
Devon: Draining commands I'll run (dry-run first):
```
./ops drain-pool --pool=pool-euc1-A --mode=graceful --grace-period=120 --parallel=4
kubectl cordon node-xxx && kubectl drain node-xxx --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Maureen: Good. Please include a pause checkpoint after every 3 racks so we can validate latency and failures. If p95 crosses 350ms, stop and roll back.
Sasha: Agreed — we'll do 3-rack batches with a 10m observation window. Also adding a safety rollback to switch traffic to us-west3 if things degrade.
Lee: Quick capacity math: impacted GPUs 144, expected spill 40% -> 58 GPUs. Warm buffer target 20% -> need ~70 GPUs total. If we don't have that in west, we should lower spill to 25% and throttle noninteractive routes.
Helen: Checking regional constraints — west3 has maintenance on 03:30-04:30 UTC (minor). Might reduce our usable headroom by ~12 GPUs between 03:30-04:30. We should avoid relying on west3 after 03:30.
Sasha: Noted — schedule: start 02:00 UTC, pause after first 3 racks at ~02:40, continue second batch 03:00. Avoid handing off to west3 after 03:20. We'll route remaining spill to dedicated-ssd-pool in us-central as fallback.
Devon: I'll stage the seed job at 01:25 UTC and run a KV sanity smoke at 01:50. Seed job: `python tools/kv_seed.py --pool=dedicated-us-central --concurrency=12 --duration=600`
ops-bot: Scheduled: maintenance-window: euc1 2025-08-12T02:00Z-04:00Z by Sasha. Task: rolling-drain pool-euc1-A/B. Ticket: MW-3489. Notifying on-call.
Maureen: Cost tradeoff choice: accept $2.1k/hr for less risk vs throttle low-priority workloads (~15% reduction) and add ~0.5s tail latency for some batch jobs. I vote throttle first, burst second.
Lee: +1 to throttle low-priority. We can reduce burst by shifting smaller models where possible.
Sasha: We'll throttle noninteractive routes by 25% and only burst if p95 > 400ms for critical routes. Everyone ok?
Devon: OK from infra ops. I'll post a runbook in #incidents with exact node lists and rollback steps.
Helen: I'll update status page and customer facing comms with the window and degraded SLO note.
Maureen: One more ask — add a quick metric to track "spill_gpu_count" and an alert threshold at >65 GPUs to auto-pause the drain.
Sasha: Will add. Runbook checklist summary (will paste in #incidents): 1) Pre-warm seed @01:25, 2) KV sanity @01:50, 3) Start drains 02:00, 3-rack batches +10m observe, 4) throttle noninteractive routes by 25%, 5) failover to us-central dedicated if west3 unavailable, 6) abort if spill_gpu_count >65 or p95>400ms.
Devon: Copy that. I'll create the runbook PR now.
ops-bot: runbook PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/762 (ops/drain-euc1).
Maureen: :thumbsup: Thanks — will monitor dashboards.
Sasha: Thanks all — will post final go/no-go 90m before window.
